text:
Oncall Bot: :rotating_light: Pager: gpu-serving queue depth > 95% in us-west-2 for the last 4m, autoscaler failing to scale (error: 'scale_limit_reached'). Possible driver flaps reported.
Alice M: I'm taking pager. ack.
Alice M: quick status — is this autoscaler unable to create nodes or are new nodes flapping on join?
Ben R: autoscaler metrics show desired=25 current=12, scale_attempts=6, last_error: quotaExceeded / provider-limit. But also saw a flurry of node terminations around same time.
Carla S: stack from node that died:
```
[  123.456789] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:00:1): 79, GPU has fallen off the bus
[  123.457000] nvidia-modeset: Unloaded
[  123.458000] kubelet: Evicting pods
```
Carla S: Xid 79 repeated on 3 different nodes in 2m. kernel OOM not obvious, but driver reset spam.
Dave K: If driver resets keep happening autoscaler sees node flapping and won't consider them healthy; effective capacity is dropping. cluster GPU count 12 -> effective 7.
Infra SRE: Confirmed: room to scale (quota) looks fine per cloud account, but provider reports a regional limit transiently returning 403 for new instances. That explains scale_limit_reached.
Alice M: So two compounding issues: 1) provider-side new-instance failures, 2) existing nodes flapping due to driver/Xid resets reducing capacity -> queue piles up -> throttling.
Customer Ops: Incident impact: elevated 5xx for embedding/large-gen routes. Two paying customers hitting degraded latency > 30s and increased error rates. CS alerted.
Ben R: Workaround idea: divert traffic to eu-central until us-west stabilizes? Need risk check on cross-region latency for these customers.
Carla S: Quick mitigation steps I'm doing: 1) disable batch-aggregation for large-gen route to reduce token pressure, 2) reduce max-concurrency per replica from 8->4, 3) mark suspect nodes unschedulable and drain long-lived jobs.
Alice M: Post commands please.
Carla S: Running:
```
kubectl cordon gpu-node-029
kubectl drain gpu-node-029 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
kubectl set env deploy/gpu-service BATCH_AGG=false --namespace=prod
kubectl scale --replicas=0 deploy/largegen-temp --namespace=prod
```
Ben R: I'm opening a provider ticket (ticket# 987654) and toggling fallback routing rule to prefer eu for non-low-latency customers.
DeployBot: Canary routing change applied to 10% of traffic -> route-us-west fallback -> eu-central.
Infra SRE: Also pushed a node pool pool-gpu-stable (older driver image) as a temporary pool to accept new instances; creating nodes there is succeeding.
Alice M: Nice. How fast can we warm pool-gpu-stable?
Infra SRE: New instances booting, kube join healthy, but we need to confirm driver stability under load. Running a smoke load test on 2 nodes now.
Carla S: Observed that most OOM/Xid events started after the 11.7 driver rollout last night. Rolling back driver on one suspect node to 11.6 and running repro.
Dave K: If rollback stops Xid events, we should do controlled rollback across affected pool and mark driver-rollout as cause.
Customer Ops: Notifying impacted customers; estimated ETA for mitigation 20-30m, will update.
Ben R: Autoscaler config note: minReplicaCreationDelay was 30s, with flapping that's too aggressive. I'm bumping to 2m to avoid thrash while provider returns capacity.
Carla S: Smoke test: on node pool-gpu-stable, 2 nodes under synthetic load stable for 6m, no Xid seen.
Alice M: Good. Next steps: 1) scale up stable pool to absorb backlog, 2) rollback driver on flapping pool, 3) keep provider ticket open and monitor new-instance success rate.
Infra SRE: Executing scale up: increasing pool-gpu-stable target from 2->8.
DeployBot: scale action queued, expected bootstrap 6-9m.
Ben R: Also enabling prefix/KV caching for frequent routing keys to reduce repeat token compute for queued requests.
Alice M: Customer Ops — can you confirm which customers saw errors and whether SLOs are impacted?
Customer Ops: Two teams reported errors: "AtlasAnalytics" and "QuickForms". Both experienced increased 500s on /v1/generate between 09:12-09:32. We will send interim status and credit offer per incident policy if >20m impact.
Carla S: Rolling back drivers on 4 flapping nodes now: patch script running.
Carla S: Patch output:
```
>> rollback-driver --node gpu-node-012 --to 11.6
... success
>> restart kubelet
```
Dave K: After rollback, gpu-node-012 reported no Xid triggers for 4m and pods rescheduled.
Infra SRE: Provider new-instance acceptance rate back to normal. Autoscaler succeeded in creating 4 more nodes and pool-gpu-stable reached 6/8.
Alice M: Observability: queue depth dropping from 98% -> 45% in 12m. Token latency P95 reduced from 18s -> 4.2s.
Customer Ops: Customers acknowledged mitigation. AtlasAnalytics still has a few failed requests but overall improving.
Ben R: Follow-ups: 1) create rollback playbook for driver rollouts, 2) add provider limit alert that triggers before scale_limit_reached, 3) audit autoscaler backoff settings.
Alice M: On-call handoff: I'm going to stay for 20m to watch for recurrence, then hand to Dave K. If anything recurs escalate to Eng-SRE.
Dave K: Taking over at +20m. Thanks team.
Oncall Bot: :white_check_mark: Incident de-escalation: queue pressure resolved, monitoring for 1h.
Customer Ops: Final note: CS will send customer postmortems and coordinate credits if needed.
Alice M: Filing incident report now and linking provider ticket 987654.
